config.title: React.memo

intro.title: React.memo
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that demonstrates how to optimize performance by preventing unnecessary re-renders, similar to the concept of React.memo in React. You will learn about pure components and change detection strategies in Angular. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript, and the OnPush change detection strategy. This will help you understand how to make your applications faster by controlling when components update.
intro.usecase: In Angular applications, change detection optimization is crucial for performance in complex UIs like data dashboards with multiple live-updating charts and tables. When you have components that display frequently changing data alongside static panels or filters, Angular's default change detection can cause unnecessary re-renders of unchanged components. Using OnPush change detection strategy helps prevent these wasteful updates, similar to how React.memo optimizes React components. This pattern is essential in enterprise applications where performance directly impacts user experience with real-time data visualization and interactive filtering systems.

objectives: Implement a functional component that accepts props and renders content
Apply React.memo to wrap a functional component for performance optimization
Construct a parent component that passes props to a memoized child component
Configure props comparison logic for React.memo when default shallow comparison is insufficient
Update state in a parent component to trigger re-renders and observe memoization effects
Bind event handlers in components to test re-render behavior with and without memoization
Control component re-renders by manipulating props passed to memoized components

steps.title: Import Component and Input from @angular/core
steps.instruction: Import the Component and Input decorators from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple named exports from the Angular core module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing decorators from Angular core
import { Component, Input } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Component and Input decorators are imported and ready to use in your Angular component.
successCriteria: Component and Input are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Component and Input from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both Component and Input from the '@angular/core' module using the import statement.

steps.title: Create a parent component class with basic structure
steps.instruction: Create a parent component class named 'ParentComponent' with the @Component decorator and an empty template.
steps.hint: Define a class with the @Component decorator above it, and include an empty template string in the decorator.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, Input } from '@angular/core';

// Create the ParentComponent class here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a ParentComponent class ready to be used as the main component in this lesson.
successCriteria: ParentComponent class is defined with @Component decorator and empty template
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both the @Component decorator and the class definition.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined a class with the @Component decorator and an empty template.

steps.title: Create a child component class with @Input property
steps.instruction: Create a child component class named ChildComponent below the ParentComponent. Add an @Input() property called 'data' of type string.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator with a selector like 'app-child' and a template that displays the data property. Remember to import Component and Input if not already done.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ChildComponent class is created with an @Input() data property that can receive string values from a parent component.
successCriteria: ChildComponent class exists with @Input() data property of type string and a basic template that uses {{ data }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added the @Input() decorator to the data property and specified its type as string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The child component isn't set up correctly. Check that you've created a class named ChildComponent with @Input() data: string and a basic template.

steps.title: Add template to child component to display input data
steps.instruction: In the ChildComponent class, add a template property that displays the value of the 'data' input property inside a paragraph element.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator's template property with backticks for multi-line strings. Reference the input property using interpolation: {{ data }}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The child component will have a template that renders the input data value when used.
successCriteria: ChildComponent has a template property containing a paragraph element with interpolation {{ data }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the template contains a paragraph element with {{ data }} interpolation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should display the 'data' input property inside a paragraph element.

steps.title: Add child component to parent template with data binding
steps.instruction: In the ParentComponent template, add the app-child selector with property binding to pass a string value to its data input.
steps.hint: Use Angular's property binding syntax: [data]="'some string value'" inside the child component selector.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Binding a string to a child component
<app-child [data]="'Hello from parent'"></app-child>
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component template now includes the child component with data binding, demonstrating how to pass data from parent to child.
successCriteria: ParentComponent template contains <app-child> with [data] property binding to a string value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the child component, but make sure to use property binding syntax [data]="'your string'".
steps.feedbackWrong: The child component isn't properly added to the parent template with data binding. Check the syntax.

steps.title: Add counter state to parent component
steps.instruction: In the ParentComponent class, add a public property named 'counter' of type number and initialize it to 0.
steps.hint: Add 'counter = 0;' inside the ParentComponent class body. Remember to include the type annotation ': number'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ParentComponent will have a counter property that can be used to track state changes and trigger re-renders.
successCriteria: ParentComponent has a public 'counter' property of type number initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but check that it's named 'counter', has type 'number', and is initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The counter property is missing or incorrect. Make sure to add 'counter: number = 0;' inside the ParentComponent class.

steps.title: Add increment button to parent template
steps.instruction: In the ParentComponent template, add a button element with the text 'Increment Counter' that will increment the counter when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a <button> tag inside the template string. You'll wire the click event in the next step.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ParentComponent template now contains a button element with the text 'Increment Counter'.
successCriteria: ParentComponent template contains a <button> element with text content 'Increment Counter'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the exact text 'Increment Counter'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ParentComponent template should contain a button element with the text 'Increment Counter'.

steps.title: Add OnPush change detection strategy to child component
steps.instruction: Add the OnPush change detection strategy to the child component's metadata to optimize its rendering behavior.
steps.hint: Import ChangeDetectionStrategy from @angular/core and add changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush to the @Component decorator of the child component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The child component will now use OnPush change detection, which only checks for changes when its input properties change or an event is triggered within the component.
successCriteria: ChangeDetectionStrategy is imported and changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush is added to the child component's @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to import ChangeDetectionStrategy from @angular/core and add the changeDetection property with the correct value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The child component doesn't have the OnPush change detection strategy. Check that you've imported ChangeDetectionStrategy and added changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush to the @Component decorator.

steps.title: Import ChangeDetectionStrategy and update imports
steps.instruction: In the import statement at the top of your file, add ChangeDetectionStrategy to the existing import from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Update the existing import line to include ChangeDetectionStrategy alongside Component and Input.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding another import to an existing statement
import { Component, Input, OnInit } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement now includes ChangeDetectionStrategy, making it available for use in the component decorator.
successCriteria: ChangeDetectionStrategy is imported from '@angular/core' along with Component and Input.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're adding ChangeDetectionStrategy to the existing import statement from '@angular/core', not creating a separate import.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement should include ChangeDetectionStrategy. Check that you've added it correctly to the existing import from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Test the optimization by observing re-render behavior
steps.instruction: Add a console.log statement inside the child component's template to observe when it re-renders.
steps.hint: Use Angular's template syntax with interpolation to call console.log inside the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The child component will log to console only when its input changes, demonstrating OnPush optimization.
successCriteria: Console.log statement is added to child template and logs only on input changes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some logging, but make sure it's inside the child component's template using interpolation syntax like {{ console.log('message') }}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The console.log statement should be added to the child component's template using Angular interpolation syntax.
